It isolates the 'propensity' term from observed TD outcomes, thereby stripping away variance due to small sample size or luck. The core operator \(\mathcal{R}_{\text{pos}}\) is a weighted sum of binary indicators, with weights derived from league statistics. This approach mirrors Bayesian hierarchical modeling where position-specific priors are applied to local data. The methodological innovation lies in treating each red-zone opportunity as an independent Bernoulli trial, then distributing league-level TD rates across defensive assignments. Critically, it avoids the pitfall of interpreting raw TD counts as direct measures of defensive effectiveness, which would be susceptible to regression to the mean. Instead, it provides a forward-looking metric that accounts for opponent offensive composition. In GSI, this translates to a conformal prediction framework where defensive performance is evaluated against position-specific baselines. In GSE, it informs state-transition models by assigning transition probabilities that reflect the expected contribution of different ball-handling roles to red-zone scoring.
